comment: Alesis ModFX Bitrman-inspired lo-fi chain whose blocks can be REORDERED. Five blocks -- bitcrush+decimate, drive, ring mod, comb, single-sideband frequency shifter -- one knob each, plus a Route knob that permutes them. The reordering is the point: crush before a comb is a different pedal from a comb before crush, and slot order in a patch reorders whole effects, never stages inside one.
gid_comment: 0x08 = Delay category, matching the rest of the release pack.
fxid_comment: 0x1D1. Free as of the 2026-08-18 fxid audit; every id in the tree is unique.

params.name: Route
params.comment: Block order, five permutations: BDRCS, SCRDB, DSBCR, RCSBD, SBRDC (B=Bits D=Drive R=Ring C=Comb S=Shift). On knob 1 deliberately -- it is the control this effect exists for, and knobs 1-2 use the verbatim-stock edit handlers.

params.name: Bits
params.comment: Word length and sample-rate decimation together, 12-bit down to 3-bit with the hold rising alongside. Defaults to a genuinely coarse setting on purpose: a fine word length makes the crusher commute with the drive (sample-and-hold and a memoryless curve give the same result either way round), which collapsed most of the Route orders into the same chain.

params.name: Drive
params.comment: Asymmetric soft clip, gain-compensated so turning it up does not just get louder.

params.name: Ring
params.comment: Ring modulator carrier, 30 Hz to ~2.2 kHz. Depth fades in from silence at 0 so the block is genuinely absent when down -- but it no longer DEFAULTS to absent, because with both Ring and Shift inert only three blocks were in the chain and Route had almost nothing left to permute.

params.name: Comb
params.comment: Short feedback comb, depth and length together. The only feedback path here, clamped below unity so no routing can make it run away.

params.name: Shift
params.comment: Single-sideband frequency shifter, centre-off. 50 is no shift; down shifts to -400 Hz, up to +400 Hz, on a squared taper so the first few Hz either side of centre are reachable. Unlike a pitch shift this ADDS a constant number of Hz, so harmonic ratios break and everything turns inharmonic and bell-like. Small shifts give a slow through-zero phasing instead.
